identity: Opening of an Arabic translation of a European scholarly monograph — Patricia Delpiano, 'العبودية في العصر الحديث' (Slavery in the Modern Age), tr. Amani Fawzi Habashi, rev. Ezzeddine Enaya. Front matter (title, author, translator, reviser) on four layout lines, then chapter heading 'الفصل الأول', section title, numbered section head '1 العبيد والخدم…', then three dense expository paragraphs on the fate of ancient slavery between Rome and the Middle Ages. A footnote marker survives as a bare '1' at @160, and a date range '500 ق م 500 م' at @177-181 and '476 م' at @211-212 are stripped parentheses.
law: §A front matter (one credit line per layout line) followed by §L/§N translated scholarly exposition. Unit here is genuinely long: ~26-27 tokens per printed sentence, held together by chained relative clauses (التي / الذي / مما / وهو ما) which are all LAW 0''' item 8 protected. What cuts is the Arabic academic register's stock of sentence-openers, and they are lexically visible: ذلك أن، بل، إن، ومن هنا فإن، لقد، أما…ف، كما (=moreover), ولكن (full form), إلا أن، and every fronted من الناحية X adverbial. Fronted adverbials take the cut BEFORE them (LAW 0''' item 9), never after.
